Joel Embiid (foot) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Raptors.

While Embiid appeared to tweak something in his left foot/ankle during Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics, his right foot has been an issue for longer. If he can’t play on Thursday, the 76ers could move Dean Wade into the starting lineup, while Jabari Walker would take on more responsibilities.
- Raphielle Johnson

    Joel Embiid (foot) recorded 16 points (2-of-9 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.

    Given the current state of Philadelphia’s center rotation, it’s been tough for Embiid to get the break he clearly needs. The former MVP has been playing through a right foot injury and appeared to tweak something in his left foot during the third quarter. And if not for an 11-of-13 night at the foul line, Embiid’s final stat line would have looked a lot worse. After Thursday’s game against the Raptors, the 76ers have a back-to-back on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Pacers before visiting the Nets. That could be a spot where the 76ers look to rest Embiid, if possible.
    - Raphielle Johnson

    Joel Embiid finished Sunday’s win over the Bulls with 18 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists and two steals.

    Coming off one of the worst games of his career, Embiid was far more impactful on Sunday. Eight of the former MVP’s 10 rebounds were on the offensive end, helping Philadelphia extend possessions and outscore Chicago 33-12 in second-chance points. This was Embiid’s third game this season with at least 10 rebounds and five assists, and his first since October 24 against the Bucks.
    - Raphielle Johnson

    Joel Embiid shot 0-of-9 from the field and 6-of-6 from the foul line in Friday’s loss to the Cavaliers, scoring six points with seven rebounds and one assist.

    With Jarrett Allen (knee) out, many fantasy managers may have expected a big night from Embiid. He didn’t come through, to say the least. Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the field, with six free throws separating him from a scoreless night. The rebounds and blocks were decent, but this was a night to forget for Embiid and those rostering him. But he wasn’t alone, as LeBron James (8/7/3/2/1) shot 3-of-12 from the field and committed six turnovers. They’ll look to bounce back on Sunday against the Bulls.
    - Raphielle Johnson

    Joel Embiid had 26 points (8-of-18 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), 15 rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s 112-106 victory over the Pistons.

    With Jalen Duren (hamstring) still out for the Pistons, Embiid had his way in the paint Wednesday. The 32-year-old center had 26 points on 18 attempts, drew five fouls and made all 10 of his free throw attempts. The 76ers have two more games this week, but with two more off days as well Embiid will have a chance to stay in the lineup.

    Embiid did not play in Saturday’s win over the Hornets, as it was Philadelphia’s second game in as many nights.
